transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Dr. Maya Patel (Verdant CTO), Liam O'Connor (Verdant Head of Security), Sofia Ramirez (Platform Eng), Ethan Cho (Legal)

Summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on compliance (SOC2/ISO), authentication (SSO/SAML), RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS options, and data retention/residency. Customer leaning towards Dedicated or Private due to PHI concerns but evaluating Hosted with VPC/Private endpoints if controls fit.

00:00:00 - Alex Turner: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate the time. quick intros - I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, with Priya and Marcus.
00:00:12 - Dr. Maya Patel: Thanks Alex, I'm Maya, CTO at Verdant Health, joined by Liam (head of security) and Sofia from platform. Ethan from legal will pop in if we need contract stuff.
00:00:22 - Priya Singh: Hi all, Priya, I'm the systems engineer, I'll run the deep tech bits.
00:00:28 - Liam O'Connor: Morning, thanks. We're fairly evaluation heavy on security controls so hoping to get into audit logs, key mgmt, and the SSO flow.
00:00:35 - Alex Turner: Totally, that's what we're here for. We'll cover SOC2/ISO evidence, SAML SSO, roles and RBAC, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, and retention and residency. Then we can map those to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment options.

00:01:05 - Sofia Ramirez: Quick context: We process PHI in a few systems, and our legal team is picky about data retention windows. We're also trying to avoid spinning up a full on-prem stack if Redwood Hosted can satisfy controls.
00:01:16 - Ethan Cho: From legal perspective, primary blockers are data residency guarantees, audit log retention for at least two years, and contractual security clauses.

00:02:10 - Priya Singh: Ok jumping in - SOC2 and ISO. Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have ISO27001 certification. we can share the certs and the SOC2 report under NDA. Our hosted environment has continuous monitoring, and Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and network isolation.
00:02:28 - Liam O'Connor: When you say "isolated GPU pools" - do you provide tenant-level network segmentation? e.g. VPC peering or private endpoints?
00:02:36 - Priya Singh: Yes - for Dedicated you get VPC peering and private subnets access. For Hosted we offer a Private Endpoint / customer-managed VPC option where the control plane is managed but network traffic goes over your VPC, and we support customer-managed routing. For fully air-gapped we have a Private on-prem package.
00:02:54 - Liam O'Connor: That helps. How about audit logs - we need immutable logs with 2 year retention and ability to stream to our SIEM.
00:03:05 - Marcus Lee: We do support audit log streaming. We can stream to customer S3 buckets or syslog/Splunk/Datadog. Logs include token-level events, model ID, request metadata, and admin actions. Retention on Redwood side is configurable but two years is usually handled by customer-managed buckets for long-term archival.
00:03:23 - Sofia Ramirez: Are the logs tamper-evident? Do you sign them or provide digests?
00:03:29 - Priya Singh: Good question - we provide signed manifests for export bundles and the audit trail is append-only within our system. For compliance-grade evidence customers typically archive to their own S3 with object lock enabled for WORM.

00:04:15 - Liam O'Connor: Encryption details - at rest and in transit. We require customer key management, KMS/HSM backed.
00:04:22 - Priya Singh: We support customer-managed keys via KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default, and a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise plans. There was a note about K-MS in the last transcript, sorry, that was a transcript artifact - we mean KMS.
00:04:42 - Alex Turner: To be explicit: in Dedicated the disk and object stores can be encrypted with your KMS; in Hosted we can configure CMKs for encryption of data-at-rest on request as part of the enterprise onboarding.

00:05:30 - Dr. Maya Patel: How about model inputs - we send in PHI for inference. Is that stored? Retention policy?
00:05:38 - Priya Singh: By default we do not persist inputs longer than needed for inference - but we have configurable retention. We can discard inputs immediately after inference or keep them only for debugging for a short window. For PHI customers we recommend Dedicated or Private and enable strict retention to zero or short retention and route audit logs to the customer.
00:05:55 - Sofia Ramirez: If we keep zero retention, do you still provide request IDs for tracing?
00:06:01 - Marcus Lee: Yes, we generate request IDs and trace data but the payload can be redacted or not stored depending on config; metadata remains for observability.

00:07:00 - Liam O'Connor: SSO/SAML - our org uses SAML 2.0 and IdP (Okta). We need SCIM for user provisioning and fine-grained RBAC.
00:07:10 - Priya Singh: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with project and route-level permissions. We can map SAML attributes to roles and sync via SCIM.
00:07:22 - Sofia Ramirez: Example roles? We need separation between devs and production ops, and audit-only roles for compliance reviewers.
00:07:30 - Priya Singh: Typical roles: Owner/Admin, Ops (deploy/rollout), Developer (invoke APIs, access dev models), Compliance (read-only audit). We can supply a JSON example of role mappings - I'll attach that.
00:07:41 - Alex Turner: (interrupting) And you can restrict per-route/model access as well so prod models require extra approvals.

00:08:15 - Ethan Cho: On contractual side, do you provide SOC2 attestation and a BAA for PHI?
00:08:22 - Alex Turner: We can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA and we do sign BAAs for PHI customers on enterprise plans (Dedicated/Private). We'll have legal follow-up from Marcus.

00:09:05 - Dr. Maya Patel: Any known customer with similar setup? healthcare customers we can reference?
00:09:12 - Marcus Lee: We have a couple healthcare customers in North America and Europe on Dedicated with KMS integrations and BAAs. We can share sanitized case studies.

00:10:00 - Priya Singh: Let's talk about network egress and model fallback. For latency sensitive calls we do smart routing, but if you need all data to stay in your region, we can pin to region-specific clusters and ensure no egress beyond customer region.
00:10:14 - Sofia Ramirez: Great. What about model hosting - do you ever have shared model cache that could leak prompts across tenants?
00:10:22 - Priya Singh: No cross-tenant KV cache. We enforce tenant isolation in cache and memory. Shared models (like open model binaries) are stored centrally, but runtime execution and KV cache are per-tenant in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we provide isolated inference contexts and logical tenancy; for the highest guarantee, Dedicated or Private provides physical isolation.

00:11:30 - Liam O'Connor: Pen testing and vuln disclosure - do you publish a bug bounty or vulnerability program?
00:11:36 - Alex Turner: We run external pentests annually and have a coordinated vulnerability disclosure program. We can also include a clause for customer-specific testing under NDA if needed.

00:12:20 - Dr. Maya Patel: What about data residencies - we need EU-only for EU patients. Does Redwood support region pinning for hosted?
00:12:27 - Priya Singh: Yes, hosted regions can be pinned. For EU-only workloads we run inference in our EU region; Dedicated can be provisioned in customer VPC in a chosen region or on-prem.

00:13:10 - Sofia Ramirez: Can we get an exported list of admin actions and who performed them? Audit log schema?
00:13:15 - Marcus Lee: Yes, logs include admin user, action, timestamp, target resource, and request ID. We'll send the schema.

00:14:05 - Liam O'Connor: Regulatory - ISO scope? Is it full platform or just control plane?
00:14:11 - Priya Singh: ISO27001 covers the control plane and operations. For Dedicated/Private the customer can extend controls to their own infra in the scope. We'll share certificates.

00:15:00 - Dr. Maya Patel: Latency vs cost tradeoff - if we go Dedicated vs Hosted with VPC, what's typical delta?
00:15:08 - Alex Turner: Usually Dedicated is more predictable with lower tail latency because of reserved GPU pools; cost is higher due to reserved capacity. Hosted with private endpoint can be cheaper but may have more variability. We can run a benchmarking session with your sample workload.
00:15:25 - Sofia Ramirez: We'll take that - please include token-level cost breakdown in the benchmark.

00:16:00 - Priya Singh: Quick note on keys and HSM: we can integrate with customer HSM for Dedicated and for Private deployments; for hosted we support customer-managed KMS, but HSM integration is part of enterprise onboarding.

00:17:30 - Ethan Cho: Contractual question: will logs we stream to our S3 remain under our control and be accessible to Redwood support?
00:17:37 - Marcus Lee: If you stream logs to your S3, Redwood does not retain a separate copy unless configured; support access can be mediated by temporary access tokens or you can provide logs on demand. We'll put that in the runbook.

00:19:00 - Dr. Maya Patel: Any differences in feature parity between Hosted and Dedicated/Private? e.g., rollouts, A/B, fast fallback?
00:19:08 - Priya Singh: Feature parity is mostly there; some advanced infra controls and deep customization (custom kernels, on-prem hardware tweaks) are only in Private. Rollouts, canaries, and A/B are supported in Hosted and Dedicated via our control plane.

00:21:00 - Sofia Ramirez: For proof-of-concept, could we do a short pilot in Hosted with CMK and VPC peering and see if legal is satisfied before committing to Dedicated?
00:21:10 - Alex Turner: Absolutely, that's a common path. We'll propose a pilot scope, duration, and success criteria.

00:22:30 - Liam O'Connor: One thing - we need encrypted audit logs with separation of duties. Can RBAC prevent support engineers from reading raw request payloads?
00:22:40 - Priya Singh: Yes. RBAC can restrict support roles from accessing payloads; they can only see metadata and error traces. Full payload access requires explicit elevated role and audit entries.

00:24:00 - Dr. Maya Patel: Suppose an incident - do you provide forensic artifacts and timelines?
00:24:07 - Marcus Lee: We provide full audit trail exports, request traces, and system metrics for investigations. We handle incident notifications as per SLA for Dedicated customers.

00:25:30 - Alex Turner: ok let's run quick live example - Priya will show a short recording of SAML login and an RBAC demo.
00:25:40 - Priya Singh: (screenshare described) login via Okta, SAML assertion mapping attributes to the Developer role, then accessing model invocation. Note: recording shows attribute mapping example, but actual production mapping will be in your IdP metadata.
00:27:10 - Sofia Ramirez: Looks good. Can we map groups to project-level permissions?
00:27:15 - Priya Singh: Yes, group->project mapping is supported.

00:29:00 - Ethan Cho: Does Redwood accept customer SOC2 clauses in the Master Services Agreement?
00:29:06 - Alex Turner: We can discuss through legal - some customers get custom clauses; typical is to exchange SOC2 under NDA and negotiate specific data residency and BAA terms. Marcus will coordinate.

00:31:00 - Dr. Maya Patel: On retention: our baseline is 30 days of raw input logs, 2 years for audit logs. Can you enforce per-project retention?
00:31:08 - Priya Singh: Yes per-project retention is configurable. For raw inputs we can set 0/7/30 days. Audit logs we encourage exporting to your own archival store for long-term retention.

00:33:00 - Liam O'Connor: Any gotchas for HIPAA? BAAs?
00:33:07 - Marcus Lee: We support BAAs for PHI and have customers under HIPAA with Dedicated deployments and stricter retention and access controls.

00:34:30 - Sofia Ramirez: Will we be able to run customer-managed model builds or fine-tuning on your infra?
00:34:37 - Priya Singh: For Dedicated yes, you can bring in custom models and we can support fine-tuning workflows with data residency controls. For hosted we have some limits and you'd need enterprise plan and review.

00:36:00 - Dr. Maya Patel: Great. Any outstanding risks?
00:36:05 - Liam O'Connor: The main risk is Hosted default key management - need to confirm CMK is available for our tenancy.
00:36:12 - Priya Singh: We'll confirm and document CMK availability for hosted pilot.

00:37:30 - Alex Turner: Recap - action items: we'll share SOC2/ISO docs under NDA, Priya will send RBAC and audit log schemas and a short demo video, Marcus to coordinate legal/BAA, and Verdant to share retention/residency policies. We'll follow up with a pilot proposal for Hosted with CMK and VPC peering and an alternative Dedicated sizing and cost.
00:37:55 - Dr. Maya Patel: Sounds good. One ask - include token-level cost estimates in the benchmarking.
00:38:02 - Alex Turner: Will do.

00:39:00 - Marcus Lee: We'll put a tentative follow-up in two weeks to review the artifacts once you have them.
00:39:10 - Sofia Ramirez: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
00:39:15 - Priya Singh: Thanks.
00:39:20 - Alex Turner: Thanks all.

(End of meeting)

Notes: Transcript includes minor transcription artifacts (e.g., K-MS vs KMS) and some speaker label ambiguity in short exchanges. References to attachments: SOC2_report.pdf (NDA), ISO27001_certificate.pdf, RBAC_sample.json, audit_log_schema.csv, pilot_proposal_draft.xlsx (links to be shared via email).
